_comment: Generated by tools/make_code_library.py - edit there, not here. Generic OBD-II code meanings with plain-English guidance; not a diagnosis. BMW's own fault code texts are proprietary and not included.

codes.title: Intake cam adjuster circuit (bank 1)
codes.meaning: Electrical fault in the circuit of the solenoid that adjusts the intake camshaft's timing (BMW calls this VANOS).
causes: Solenoid connector loose, corroded or full of oil
Wiring between the solenoid and the engine computer
checks: Check the solenoid's connector for oil, corrosion or damage
Measure the solenoid's resistance against the specification
Check the wiring back to the engine computer
codes.drive: Usually drivable, but power and smoothness can suffer. Get it checked soon.
codes.ignored: Rough running, less power and higher fuel use.

codes.title: Intake cam timing over-advanced or performance (bank 1)
codes.meaning: The intake camshaft isn't reaching the timing the engine computer asks for.
causes: Low, old or wrong engine oil (VANOS runs on oil pressure)
Sticking or dirty intake VANOS solenoid
Worn or stretched timing chain, guides or tensioner
Faulty intake VANOS adjuster or camshaft sensor
checks: Check the oil level and when the oil was last changed
Look for other cam or crank timing codes: several together point to the timing chain
Inspect, clean or replace the intake VANOS solenoid
Have the cam timing checked if the code comes back
codes.drive: Usually drivable with less power. Get it checked soon; if the engine rattles or runs badly, don't drive hard.
codes.ignored: If the cause is a worn timing chain, it can eventually cause serious engine damage.

codes.title: System too lean (bank 1)
codes.meaning: The engine is getting more air or less fuel than expected, and the engine computer has reached its limit for adding fuel.
causes: Vacuum or boost leak (hoses, intake gasket)
Crankcase ventilation fault, often in the valve cover
Low fuel pressure (fuel pump or filter)
Air flow or manifold pressure sensor reading wrong
Exhaust leak before the front oxygen sensor
checks: Listen for hissing at idle and check intake and charge hoses
Smoke test the intake for leaks
Check fuel pressure, low and high side
Watch fuel trims in live data at idle and under load
codes.drive: Usually drivable. Get it checked soon, and avoid hard driving if the engine also misfires.
codes.ignored: Misfires, and on a turbo engine, running lean under heavy load raises the risk of knock and engine damage.

codes.title: System too rich (bank 1)
codes.meaning: The engine is getting more fuel than expected, and the engine computer has reached its limit for taking fuel away.
causes: Fuel vapor purge valve stuck open
Air flow or pressure sensor reading wrong
checks: Look for other injector or purge codes
Watch fuel trims in live data
Check fuel pressure
Check that the purge valve closes
codes.drive: Usually fine to drive gently. Get it checked soon.
codes.ignored: Higher fuel use, fouled spark plugs and, over time, a damaged catalytic converter.
